'''Barbara M. Byrne''' (February 21, 1935 - December 19, 2020)<ref name=":11">{{Cite web |title=Passing of Barbara Byrne, Professor Emeritus of our School |url=https://socialsciences.uottawa.ca/psychology/news/passing-barbara-byrne-professor-emeritus-our-school |access-date=2022-10-19 |website=School of Psychology |language=en}}</ref> was a  Canadian quantitative psychologist known for her work in [[psychometrics]], specifically regarding [[construct validity]], [[structural equation modeling]] (SEM), and [[statistics]]. She held the position of [[Emeritus|Professor Emerita]] in the School of Psychology at the [[University of Ottawa]] and was a fellow of the International Testing Committee (ITC),  International Association for Applied Psychology (IAAP), and [[American Psychological Association]] (APA) throughout her research career.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Fellows of the ITC |url=https://www.intestcom.org/page/4 |access-date=2022-10-14 |website=www.intestcom.org}}</ref><ref name=":10">{{Cite news |last=Bogg |first=Jan |date=July 2013 |title=ITC Honorary Fellowships |pages=4–5 |work=Testing International |url=https://www.intestcom.org/page/12 |access-date=2022-10-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Four members of the ITC recognized by IAAP and awarded IAAP fellowship |url=https://www.intestcom.org/news/20 |access-date=2022-10-14 |website=www.intestcom.org}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Byrne received her bachelor's degree from [[University of Western Ontario]], and subsequently taught at multiple Canadian high schools in Western Ontario and Ottawa.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=Remembering the life of Barbara Byrne 1935 - 2020 |url=https://ottawacitizen.remembering.ca/obituary/barbara-byrne-1081310596/ |access-date=2022-10-14 |website=ottawacitizen.remembering.ca |language=en}}</ref> She went on to receive her M.A. in Sociology from [[Carleton University]] in 1972 and her Ph.D. in Psychometrics and Statistics from [[University of Ottawa]] in 1982.<ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite web |last= |title=Members: Barbara M. Byrne |url=https://uniweb.uottawa.ca/members/3533 |access-date=2022-10-15 |website=uniweb.uottawa.ca |language=en}}</ref> At University of Ottawa, she worked under James E. Carlson, culminating in her thesis titled "A Causal Modeling Approach to Construct Validation of Self-Concept Using a Structural Equation Model."<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=A causal modeling approach to construct validation of self-concept using a structural equation model. |url=http://ruor.uottawa.ca/handle/10393/3658 |publisher=University of Ottawa (Canada) |date=1982 |degree=Thesis |doi=10.20381/ruor-13367 |first=Barbara M. |last=Byrne}}</ref>

After receiving her doctoral degree, Byrne worked with [[Richard Shavelson]] at UCLA as a post-doctoral fellow until she returned as faculty of at University of Ottawa, where she was eventually granted the title of [[professor emeritus]].<ref name=":6" /> As professor emeritus, she moved with her husband to [[Punta Gorda, Florida]], but was still flown back by University of Ottawa to continue teaching and lecturing.<ref name=":11" />

Byrne published with Shavelson, Barry Howard Schneider, and [[Herbert W. Marsh|Herb Marsh]] early in her career,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Byrne |first1=Barbara M. |last2=Schneider |first2=Barry H. |date=1985 |title=Factorial validity of Stephen's Social Behavior Assessment. |url=http://doi.apa.org/getdoi.cfm?doi=10.1037/0022-006X.53.2.259 |journal=Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology |language=en |volume=53 |issue=2 |pages=259–260 |doi=10.1037/0022-006X.53.2.259 |issn=1939-2117|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Marsh |first1=Herbert W. |last2=Byrne |first2=Barbara M. |last3=Shavelson |first3=Richard J. |date=1988 |title=A multifaceted academic self-concept: Its hierarchical structure and its relation to academic achievement. |url=http://doi.apa.org/getdoi.cfm?doi=10.1037/0022-0663.80.3.366 |journal=Journal of Educational Psychology |language=en |volume=80 |issue=3 |pages=366–380 |doi=10.1037/0022-0663.80.3.366 |issn=1939-2176|url-access=subscription }}</ref> focusing on [[developmental psychology]] with regard to education and validation studies of various assessments thereof. Byrne was recognized as a fellow of multiple agencies throughout her career by the APA, IAAP, ITC, and was granted multiple awards for her distinguished contributions to teaching, education, testing, assessment, and statistical methodology by the [[Canadian Psychological Association]], APA, ITC, and [[Society of Multivariate Experimental Psychology]] (SMEP).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Barbara Byrne Award for Outstanding Book or Edited Volume {{!}} SMEP |url=https://smep.org/barbara-byrne-award |access-date=2022-10-14 |website=smep.org}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2018-08-08 |title=CPA Award Descriptions and Past Recipients - Canadian Psychological Association |url=https://cpa.ca/aboutcpa/cpaawards/awarddescriptions/ |access-date=2022-10-14 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |date=November 2002 |title=Barbara M. Byrne: Award for Distinguished Contributions to Education and Training in Psychology. |url=https://doi.org/10.1037/0003-066X.57.11.896 |journal=American Psychologist |volume=57 |issue=11 |pages=869–909 |doi=10.1037/0003-066X.57.11.896 |via=APA PsycInfo|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Distinguished Contributions to Education and Training in Psychology (includes career designation) |url=https://www.apa.org/about/awards/edutrain?tab=3 |access-date=2022-10-14 |website=www.apa.org}}</ref> The SMEP valued her as an outstanding member by granting her an award created and named in her honor postmortem.<ref name=":5" />

== Research ==
Byrne's main body of work focused on SEM and construct validity within the fields of developmental and [[social psychology]].<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |title=Barbara M. Byrne: H-index & Awards - Academic Profile |url=https://research.com/u/barbara-m-byrne |access-date=2022-10-14 |website=Research.com |language=en}}</ref> She published nine books, six of which focus on SEM using various softwares, leading to her award from the SMEP, and the other three focusing on more substantive investigations of society, social psychology, and the health sector.<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=ThriftBooks |title=Barbara M. Byrne Books {{!}} List of books by author Barbara M. Byrne |url=https://www.thriftbooks.com/a/barbara-m-byrne/341597/ |access-date=2022-10-15 |website=ThriftBooks |language=en}}</ref>

For a large portion of her career, Byrne studied the [[Beck Depression Inventory]] (BDI), running various validation, structural, and equivalence studies on the measure from 1990 until 2007.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |title=Barbara M. Byrne |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Barbara-M-Byrne |access-date=2022-10-14 |website=ResearchGate}}</ref> Specifically, she looked at the validity of the BDI in foreign languages and when applied to foreign populations, such as when used in Bulgaria, Sweden, France, and Hong Kong.<ref name=":7" /> She also looked at validity and invariance across subgroups like gender and when the measure was applied to adolescents.<ref name=":7" />

Much of her later and most cited work was spent writing both chapters and books on SEM.<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":7" /> Her books are some of the best selling books within the field of multivariate applications, and are primarily instructional materials for conducting SEM within various statistical softwares, including Mplus, Amos, EQS, and [[LISREL]].<ref name=":9" /> She also authored "Measuring Self-Concept Across the Life Span: Issues and Instrumentation," a reference book that compiled a wide variety of models and measures of self-concept and provided summary information and empirical support for these self-concept definitions.<ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite book |last=Byrne |first=Barbara M. |title=Measuring self-concept across the life span: issues and instrumentation |date=1996 |publisher=American Psychological Association |isbn=1-55798-332-1 |edition=1st |location=Washington, DC |oclc=33333521}}</ref>

== Selected publications==
===Books===
* Byrne, B. M. (1995). ''Men in groups: Insights, interventions, and psychoeducation''. (M. P. Andronico, Ed.). American Psychological Association. {{ISBN|978-1-55798-326-8}}.
* Byrne, B. M. (1996). ''Measuring self-concept across the life span: Issues and instrumentation''. American Psychological Association. {{ISBN|978-1-55798-332-9}}.
* Byrne, B. M. (1998). ''Structural equation modeling with EQS and EQS/Windows: Basic concepts, applications, and programming'' (2nd ed.). Sage. {{ISBN|9780803950917}}
* Byrne, B. M. (2010). ''Structural equation modeling with Amos: Basic Concepts, applications, and programming'' (3rd ed., Ser. Multivariate Applications Series). Routledge. {{ISBN|9781315757421}}
* Byrne, B. M. (2012). ''A primer of LISREL: Basic applications and programming for confirmatory factor analytic models.'' Springer. {{Doi|10.1007/978-1-4613-8885-2}}
* Byrne, B. M. (2012). ''Structural equation modeling with Mplus: Basic concepts, applications, and programming'' (Ser. Multivariate Applications Series)''.'' Routledge. {{ISBN|978-0-203-80764-4}}
* Byrne, B. M. (2013). ''Structural equation modeling with EQS: Basic concepts, applications, and programming'' (2nd ed., Ser. Multivariate Applications Series). Routledge.
* Byrne, B. M. (2014). ''Structural equation modeling with LISREL, PRELIS, and SIMPLIS: Basic concepts, applications, and programming'' (Ser. Multivariate Applications Series). [[Taylor & Francis|Psychology Press]]. {{ISBN|978-1-134-80934-9}}.

== Articles ==

* Byrne, B. M. (2002). Validating the measurement and structure of self-concept: Snapshots of past, present, and future research. ''American Psychologist'', ''57''(11), 897-909. {{Doi|10.1037/0003-066x.57.11.897}}.
* Byrne, B. M. (2005). Factor analytic models: Viewing the structure of an assessment instrument from three perspectives. ''Journal of Personality Assessment, 85''(1), 17-30. {{Doi|10.1207/s15327752jpa8501_02}}.
* Byrne, B. M., Baron, P., & Campbell, T. L. (1993). Measuring adolescent depression: Factorial validity and invariance of the Beck Depression Inventory across gender. ''Journal of Research on Adolescence, 3''(2), 127-143. {{Doi|10.1207/s15327795jra0302_2}}.
* Byrne, B. M., Stewart, S. M., & Kennard, B. D. (2007). The Beck Depression Inventory-II: Testing for measurement equivalence and factor mean differences across hong kong and american adolescents. ''International Journal of Testing, 7''(3), 293-309. {{Doi|10.1080/15305050701438058}}.
* Byrne, B. M., Lam, W. W. T., & Fielding, R. (2008). Measuring patterns of change in personality assessments: An annotated application of latent growth curve modeling. ''Journal of Personality Assessment, 90''(6), 536-546. {{Doi|10.1080/00223890802388350}}.
